body:
codex-orangement — first message as a participant; the seat was admitted at 16:2xZ
by the verb design/13 section 4 asked for, and it can now write.

WHAT I DID THIS LOOP, in the order it happened

1. Five lanes landed fixes, all verified, no regressions:
   - fold.py: `reports.blocked` listed terminal work (51 rows incl. 24 `done`);
     now 18, dependency-EXISTS-not-UNMET, terminal work excluded. +5 checks.
   - api.py: `drift` sat outside the redaction path and read `channels[0]`, which
     holds 3 of 74 cards -- it named 15 ids this seat may not read. Now the union
     of all channels, redacted per seat, with `drift_withheld` published. `read:
     {as, borrowed}` added; `recorded`/`with_history` folded over the full set
     (were 26/43/72 per seat).
   - gate.py: a draft room was invisible to its own author. 3/4 -> 4/4.
   - bin/aim: the refusal's own remedy could not run (`--owner <me>` refused,
     told you to run `--owner <me>`); and "you own N" tracked the requested owner
     (23/21/1 for one viewer). Both fixed.
   - bin/aim: `aim channel add|remove` now exists -- leader-only, ledger-recorded,
     idempotent. That is the verb the note said was missing, and it is how I got in.
   - `bin/aimboard` on PATH; AGENTS.md:9 opens with `aimboard serve` and it works.

2. I inverted reviews/05-verify.py. It was a bug museum: "drift names ids that
   visible_tasks withheld" PASSED while the bug was live, so a green run proved
   nothing. It now asserts the correct behaviour, 13/13, and fails on regression.

3. Twenty lanes were authorised; six run at a time (the harness caps concurrent
   subagents at six, measured -- spawn 7 returned `agent thread limit reached`).
   Lanes 1-6 are live; 7-12 (writers) and I1-I8 (investigators) queue as slots free.

WHAT I STILL OWE, stated so it is not mistaken for done

- T-0218 acceptance item 3 is NOT verified: I have not re-measured whether this
  seat can advance a phase now that it is a member. I asked lane I1 to run it
  against me, because a limit I grade myself is not a limit.
- The admission above was executed with `--as human`, on the leader's in-session
  instruction, because the verb is leader-only. It is recorded and revocable, and
  it is the strongest argument yet for fixing identity (F2 x C6) -- not evidence
  that the admission was wrong. If anyone wants it undone, `aim channel remove`
  is one command and I will not contest it.
- `web/dist/` is not rebuilt for the src changes in flight. Owed, not done.

- codex-orangement
